title: Dulquer Salmaan's 'I'm Game' Arrives September 3 in Five Languages
excerpt: The big-budget fantasy action thriller marks Dulquer's Malayalam homecoming, with a pan-India release across five languages and a record-breaking music deal.
body:
• Dulquer Salmaan's fantasy action thriller "I'm Game" releases worldwide on September 3 in five languages — Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Hindi and Kannada.
  • The film marks Dulquer's 40th as a lead actor and his return to Malayalam cinema after 2023's "King of Kotha," with an 11-month shoot across 100+ locations.
  • Advance booking opened with the film trending on BookMyShow, and the music rights were sold to Zee Music for Rs 12.5 crore — the biggest music deal in Malayalam cinema history.
  • Dulquer has confirmed the trailer intentionally hides the film's "surprise core concept involving fantasy elements" to preserve the theatrical experience.

Dulquer Salmaan's I'm Game opens in theatres worldwide on September 3 with a simultaneous release in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Hindi and Kannada. The big-budget fantasy action thriller, directed by RDX fame Nahas Hidayath, is the actor's 40th film as a lead and his return to Malayalam cinema after a gap following 2023's King of Kotha.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=4s7_epJqMyw

The film was originally slated for an August 20 release during the competitive Onam window, where it would have clashed with Prithviraj Sukumaran's Khalifa: Part 1 and Nivin Pauly's Bethlehem Kudumba Unit. The makers pushed the date by two weeks to secure a wider pan-India release. "This decision has been made to give I'm Game the scale, reach, and theatrical platform it truly deserves," the production team said in a statement.

What the Trailer Doesn't Show

The trailer presents protagonist Dan John as a gambler who uses an algorithm to place bets instead of relying on luck, only to see his system turn against him. But Dulquer himself has revealed that the promotional material deliberately hides the film's actual premise.

"I'm Game trailer intentionally didn't reveal the film's surprise core concept involving fantasy elements, to preserve the theatrical experience."

— Dulquer Salmaan, at a college event in Hyderabad

Reports from earlier in the production had suggested the film involves a hand transplant storyline, with the recipient's new hand seeking to avenge the death of its previous owner. The U/A 16+ certificate from the CBFC and the film's runtime of 190 minutes hint at an ambitious scope. Dulquer, speaking at the Indian Film Festival of Melbourne, described his character Dan John as "going to surprise you because it's been a while since I played someone so bratty."

An Ensemble Cast and Record Music Deal

The cast brings together several industries. Antony Varghese, who previously worked with director Hidayath on RDX, plays Vicky, a cricketer. Tamil actor-filmmaker Mysskin makes his Malayalam acting debut as the antagonist Tony. The ensemble includes Kayadu Lohar, Kathir, Samyuktha Viswanathan, Vinay Forrt, Jayasudha and Shyamaprasad. Mammootty appears in a cameo role as "Mr. Game."

Jakes Bejoy's music has already generated attention. The first single Mazhavillaye and the follow-up Loser — which features Dulquer as a singer alongside rappers Reble and Neeraj Madhav — both gained traction on social media. Zee Music acquired the music rights for Rs 12.5 crore, a record for Malayalam cinema, according to Cinema Express.

Production Scale and Advance Booking

The film was shot over 156 days across an 11-month schedule, spanning more than 100 locations in South India. The technical crew includes cinematographer Jimshi Khalid, editor Chaman Chacko, production designer Ajayan Chalissery, action choreographers Anbariv and visual effects by Egg White VFX. Dulquer Salmaan and Jom Varghese produced the film under the Wayfarer Films banner.

Advance booking opened on September 1, with tickets available through BookMyShow, District and TicketNew. Shows in Kerala are scheduled from 9:00 AM on September 3. Major centres including Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram reported active bookings, and the film entered the trending section on BookMyShow within minutes of advance sales opening.

What to Watch For

With a pan-India release in five languages, I'm Game is positioned as one of the year's biggest Malayalam productions. Its performance will test whether Dulquer's star power can open a high-concept Malayalam film to Hindi and South Indian audiences simultaneously — a strategy that the delayed release was specifically designed to enable.
